title: Which AIs have you used? How were they?
author: MichaelEmouse
selftext:
Which AIs have been most useful to you?

If you've used a paid tier of one of the main AIs, how was it? 

If you used more than one, how did they compare?

comments.author: Illustrious_Pay_2657
comments.body:
It depend on what field you are applying the AI to, so far i tried this for web, automation and gaming and i think  tools that uses Gimini or OpenAI should be suffisent for small to medium tasks.  
I lately come across Bezi a tool dedicated to unity, the free tier basically help you plan small things but the paid tier (i am in advanced) make your life esier, but like any other agent based tool, its best if you know what you are doing as they can easly remove and alter things without your awarness.

comments.author: HONGSHIreddit
comments.body:
For game dev coding, I tried Claude and Bezi. I initially tried Claude because it was free to use and I don't know coding so a lot of my friends would say Claude is great for that. I tried it and it was getting things to "work" but the more scripts I generated, it would break the game. 

Then I came across Bezi while searching for AI for unity development and they marketed in a way where it was appealing to my needs lol. They said it uses project context, good for scripting, and built for unity so I gave it a try and the codes that Claude made for me with game breaking issues, Bezi fixed those up. 

It was a no brainer for me to use this for my project lol. They've updated a lot of useful features since then so I'm truly finding a lot of worth in it.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
My workflow has been Godot for my game engine, ChatGPT plus because it gives access to codex and cursor. Cursor on auto mode so I think it uses chat gpt and codex. I actually have chat help me come up with prompts for cursor lol.

Seems to all work really well! I have cursor (codex) go back and forth to refine changes to my scripts (in plan mode in cursor) before I let it implement the changes.  

While my game is a simple platformer with mini games (the minigames are seemingly more complicated than the main game actually) but so far the success rate of changes to code without bugs is probably like 80% which seems good to me. 

Im not utilizing these tools in as clever way as my friend is even and it seems to be working really well!

comments.author: LL555LL
comments.body: Claude paid. Great when given a good prompt, which is a step in my workflow I'm building (using a different AI to help me make better prompts)

replies.author: MichaelEmouse
replies.body:
What tends to make for a good prompt?

  
Which AI do you use to make prompts? Could you use Claude to help you make prompts for Claude?

replies.author: LL555LL
replies.body:
You can, but in a different window. 

I use Chatgpt to refine prompts. It's actually REALLY good at that . And then bam, get WAY better results in Claude. The key is keeping it two separate chats with the same background different contrxt

comments.author: Ok-Antelope7968
comments.body: Claude code only for coding is what I been using

comments.author: Worried_Initial3633
comments.body: Claude for code, Hunyan for 3D… dm for workflows

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
Github copilot coding agent with GPT4.1 and claude sonnet 4.x for code generation, also for generation of some simpler images and for lottie animations. It can generate QR codes without any problems, too.
The coding agent works in a way that you write issues in github and tell the agent to work on the issue. It creates a branch and a pull request (PR) then.  
So the agent is encapsulated and cannot do harm. In the worst case, I have to delete a branch and PR.
As with human developers, it is important to have tasks that are not too large to get good results.

For Images, I use the Flux1.dev and now Flux2.dev for stable diffusion and the free GPU time from huggingface.co

comments.author: UmpireGaming
comments.body:
Over the past year and a half I used all of the vibe coding apps initially but landed on these as my main game building tools:

Replit.ai - this is the platform I landed on for hosting the applications I built and I've just found it to be the most friendly with preview and I like being able to have the all-in-one package for deployment. If you use the replit agent cost can get out of hand so you want to go in knowing how to use it. 

Claude Code - I have been using this for my coding agent for over a year now after trying many of them and would not suggest any others over claude. You can use Claude inside of your replit shell and just start small with learning to work with it. 

Leonardo AI - I use this for all of my image creation from characters, buildings, really any ui I want to create. 

Ludo.ai - this is the best I have found for character sprites but to be honest this is one part I almost still lean towards hiring someone to do or learning more about how to make sprites. 

I spend $150 per month on all these but replit and Claude would be the two I would recommend the most. 

Good luck with whatever you are starting and I am sure there will be many other great suggestions!
